detail.longDescription: Let's say I have a web scraping pipeline. For some reason, I use Celery to write a sanitized payload to the database. The payload is a list for rows. Due to the nature of the problem, two Celery tasks may partially share rows. Is there a way to merge two Celery tasks into one, where I can merge the rows and deduplicate? Even if deduplication is not necessary, It will be nice to do bulk write. I am not interested in the upsert-or-ignore database scenario. @app.task def save_rows(rows): sanitized_rows = sanitize(rows) bulk_write_to_database(sanitized_rows) # Payload received from the scraping pipeline A rows_a = [ {"url": "/article/1", "title": "Article 1"}, {"url": "/article/2", "title": "Article 2"}, ] # Payload received from the scraping pipeline B rows_b = [ {"url": "/article/2", "title": "Article 2"}, {"url": "/article/3", "title": "Article 3"}, ] save_rows.delay(rows_a) save_rows.delay(rows_b)
